related_questions.question: What are the ingredients in a vaccine?

text_blocks.snippet: Vaccines typically contain antigens, adjuvants, preservatives, stabilizers, and trace amounts of manufacturing byproducts. The main ingredient, the antigen, is a weakened or inactive part of a pathogen that triggers an immune response. Adjuvants help boost the immune response, while preservatives and stabilizers ensure the vaccine's safety and effectiveness.
snippet_highlighted_words: antigens, adjuvants, preservatives, stabilizers, and trace amounts of manufacturing byproducts

list.title: Antigens:
list.snippet: These are the active components of the vaccine that stimulate the immune system to recognize and fight off the pathogen. They can be whole, weakened (attenuated), or inactive viruses or bacteria, or just parts of these like proteins or sugars.

list.title: Adjuvants:
list.snippet: These ingredients enhance the immune response to the antigen, sometimes allowing for a lower dose of the antigen to be used.

list.title: Preservatives:
list.snippet: Preservatives, like thimerosal, are used in multi-dose vials to prevent contamination and extend the vaccine's shelf life.

list.title: Stabilizers:
list.snippet: Stabilizers, like gelatin, help maintain the vaccine's structure and prevent it from breaking down during storage.

list.title: Manufacturing Byproducts:
list.snippet: Trace amounts of substances used during the manufacturing process, like egg protein or formaldehyde, may be present in some vaccines.

list.title: mRNA:
list.snippet: Some newer vaccines, like the mRNA COVID-19 vaccines, use mRNA as the active ingredient. This mRNA provides instructions for the body to produce the antigen.

list.title: Lipids:
list.snippet: Lipids (oils) are used in some mRNA vaccines to encapsulate and protect the mRNA.

list.title: Sugars and Salts:
list.snippet: Sugars like sucrose and salts are used to help maintain the vaccine's stability and pH levels.
